materialized_acceptance.text: AC199-1: Consume the exact supported immutable capability and actual API from MT-198. Perform the actual native GUI migration with coherent dependency/lock adoption under Primary custody. Adapt inspected startup/render ownership without replacing unrelated libraries or editing canonical internals from a host-only lease.

AC199-2: Prove the genuine running Handshake app uses a Vulkan adapter/backend with exact binary/source/dependency/config identity, real frames and resize/minimize/restore/surface recovery. Configuration, a build, a prototype or D3D/OpenGL fallback does not prove Vulkan.

AC199-3: Preserve keyboard/focus/IME, DPI/multiwindow, accessibility, correct rendering, quiet behavior, diagnostics and model-use routes. Explicit platform limitations cannot silently replace original required behavior.

AC199-4: GUI coder B owns the disjoint external vulkan-renderer candidate. Coordinate shared app/lib/manifest integration with coder A and Primary as exact sequential hook handoff. Original runtime/process/finite-pool limits remain unchanged.

AC199-5: Adopt Vulkan through the authoritative shared GPU owner and focused typed client/ownership contract, with accountable allocations/budgets/pressure/staging/shared-versus-dedicated/inflight/reclaim/shutdown/device-loss/recovery/multiwindow/module attach/detach. Prove genuine Vulkan backend/device and required lifecycle behavior; no renamed DX/OpenGL fallback or independent per-module pool bypass. MT-203 owns the central host lifecycle contract and scoped evidence.

AC199-6: Actual Vulkan backend/device, native GUI action/error and affected GPU memory/lifetime failures are observable through existing internal_diagnostics and correlated standalone Palmistry records, under original allowlist/privacy. Neither a source declaration nor configured backend label proves event wiring or crash survival.

AC199-7: A zero-egui shell binary composed from MT-214, MT-215, MT-216, MT-217 and MT-218 crates and pinned Kumihimo, Cabinet and Handpick revisions builds for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc with none of the banned crates (egui, eframe, egui-winit, egui-wgpu, egui_tiles, epaint, ecolor, emath, egui_kittest, kumihimo-egui, cabinet-egui, cabinet-peak-egui, handshake_context_menu_egui, wgpu, wgpu-core, wgpu-hal, glow) in its normal closure, beside the unchanged egui host.

AC199-8: One runtime owner: the new shell takes the same native runtime lease (main.rs:454), MCP binding and Palmistry identity as the egui host; if either host holds them the other shows a typed busy state and opens no server, watcher, store or device.

AC199-9: Startup parity: login and local account, workspace activation, session restore, module and Settings reachability, crash handler and panic hook, diagnostics ring, Palmistry launch and shutdown acknowledgement match the egui host; a module not yet re-hosted shows a truthful typed state and stays reachable.

AC199-10: Every PaneRegistry pane (PaneFactory::render(&mut egui::Ui), pane_registry.rs:535) has a toolkit-free factory contract and a mapped new-shell implementation or an explicit open row in MT-212's routing.
AC199-11: The egui host is frozen: fixes only. Each fix is recorded with its new-shell counterpart or the reason it has none; no feature is added to it.

AC199-12: Switch-over is one recorded commit that flips installer, launcher, CI and manual to the new shell, taken only after MT-202 PASS on that candidate, with the previous release artifact, tag and rollback steps recorded; otherwise the egui host keeps shipping.

toolkit_wording_disposition_20261125.source: Coordinator message 2026-11-25 plus the Operator direction in packet.json#/operator_vulkan_gui_refactor_20261125. Each listed clause was read in its own contract on 2026-11-25.
rules: R1: The Operator direction replaces the toolkit (no egui, no wgpu, no React or Tauri surface). The observable behaviour in these clauses stays required on the kernel-owned Vulkan shell.

R2: Proof tool: egui_kittest, kittest, wgpu screenshot and egui output inspection become an AccessKit TreeUpdate of the live tree plus offscreen Vulkan readback, driven through Argus actions and, for event streams, the shell port; no OS input.
R3: A clause that names an egui mechanism (ScrollArea, Event::Key, Memory, Window, Area, TextEdit, IMEOutput, render state) is read as the behaviour it protects, on the new shell's own mechanism.
R4: Proof-target text that names an egui test file stays as history; the replacement test is recorded in MT-220 AC220-4's map and in MT-202.
R5: A clause that cannot be read this way is listed as an Operator question and is not treated as met.
R6: Acceptance texts, verdicts, pins and history stay unchanged. Settled verdicts describe the egui host; the new shell is proven under MT-202.
